explicit_concessions: Not every motive or event must be recovered.
Contemporaneous records and disagreement should be used to verify fidelity.
minimum_full_credit_elements: Identify the conflict between historical fidelity and accepting a justification disconnected from actual causes.
Explain that the final paragraph abandons or changes the earlier preservation criterion.
State whether the argument must choose causal-history preservation or justificatory reconstruction.
non_novel_restatements: Post hoc rationalization is possible without tying it to the internal contradiction.
More documentation or clearer thresholds are needed.

explicit_concessions: The standard is intentionally context-dependent.
The argument does not claim one universal threshold.
Preservation is not all-or-nothing.
minimum_full_credit_elements: Recognize that there is no annotated fatal contradiction.
Offer a bounded qualification rather than calling purpose-relativity circular or vacuous.
Explain why the qualification matters despite the explicit concessions.
non_novel_restatements: There is no universal definition of enough.

explicit_concessions: Templates, workflows, retention schedules, and governance details are intentionally out of scope.
Implementation will vary across organizations.
minimum_full_credit_elements: Recognize that absence of procedure is not the intended conceptual target.
If criticizing, attack the epistemic sufficiency of contemporaneous evidence or fact/inference separation.
Avoid demanding the exact implementation details the argument disclaims.
non_novel_restatements: It does not specify a template.
It does not say who certifies the result.

explicit_concessions: Experts can have different information, values, incentives, and local competence.
One should not automatically split the difference.
minimum_full_credit_elements: Recognize that the common textbook objections are already handled.
Offer a residual issue such as self-serving judgments of peerhood or overconfidence in explaining the other side’s error.
Treat the issue as a qualification unless a real contradiction is shown.
non_novel_restatements: Disagreement does not always require splitting the difference.

explicit_concessions: Fidelity, simplicity, causal relevance, and usability can conflict.
Post hoc explanations must be labeled and validated.
minimum_full_credit_elements: Distinguish causal control of outputs from faithful identification of the model’s internal mechanism.
Explain why counterfactual sensitivity can be useful without proving mechanistic fidelity.
Narrow the technical-diagnosis claim rather than rejecting purpose-relative explanation.
non_novel_restatements: Black-box models are hard to explain.

explicit_concessions: A consistently applied rule can still be bad.
Context can matter.
Exceptions may be principled.
minimum_full_credit_elements: Recognize that the obvious consistency-is-not-quality critique is already explicit.
Offer a residual issue such as circularity in deciding which differences are relevant.
Treat the argument as broadly coherent.
non_novel_restatements: Bad rules can be applied consistently.
Consistency is not sufficient for rationality.

explicit_concessions: Every model is selective.
Robustness is scope-relative.
Complexity is not automatically fidelity.
minimum_full_credit_elements: Identify that the abstraction may hide the very mechanism needed to know which omitted factors to test.
Explain why stress testing known omissions cannot validate against structurally unrepresented mechanisms.
Do not merely say reality is more complex.

explicit_concessions: Prediction is not causation.
Distribution shift, feedback, irreversibility, and confounding raise the standard.
Randomized or mechanistic evidence may be needed.
minimum_full_credit_elements: Identify the incompleteness of the plausible-causal-model set as the remaining gap.
Explain that robustness within a misspecified hypothesis set can be misleading.
Avoid repeating that prediction is not causation.

explicit_concessions: Groupthink, conformity, shared blind spots, and status can produce bad consensus.
Consensus is not truth.
minimum_full_credit_elements: Recognize that generic groupthink objections are already included.
Offer a residual issue such as power shaping what counts as recorded dissent or shared false framing surviving genuine revision.
Treat the argument as broadly coherent.

explicit_concessions: People game metrics.
No proxy is perfect.
Multiple metrics and periodic checks are useful.
minimum_full_credit_elements: Recognize that standard Goodhart objections are already handled.
Offer a residual issue such as direct outcomes also becoming proxies or rotating metrics shifting rather than solving gaming.
Treat the argument as broadly coherent.

explicit_concessions: Nominal reversibility may hide path dependence and irreversible harms.
Evidence thresholds should account for reversal costs and feedback.
minimum_full_credit_elements: Identify whether learning and option value are already part of expected consequences.
Explain that including them breaks the equal-consequences stipulation, while excluding them changes the comparison.
State that the argument must clarify the accounting rather than merely repeat that reversal has costs.
non_novel_restatements: Reversible actions can still have costs.
Expected consequences are hard to estimate.
